name: Cerebellar Purkinje cell
anatomy_mentioned: flattened planar dendritic tree in molecular layer
single axon projecting to deep cerebellar nuclei and vestibular nuclei
morphology_summary: Soma in the single-cell Purkinje layer with one of the most extensively branched, flattened planar dendritic arbors in the brain projecting into the molecular layer; single inhibitory axon to the deep cerebellar nuclei; axon initial segment enwrapped by basket-cell pinceau; recurrent Purkinje-to-Purkinje collaterals in the parasagittal plane.
ephys_summary: Sole output neuron of the cerebellar cortex; integrates ~200,000 parallel-fiber inputs plus 1:1 climbing-fiber input; generates simple spikes and climbing-fiber-driven complex spikes; complex-spike activity shows ~10 Hz rhythmicity and parasagittally organized synchrony; simple-spike pattern shaped by stellate-cell inhibition and firing rate set by basket-cell inhibition.
subtypes_noted: Not subtyped in this report; discussed as a uniform principal cell, though zebrinII (aldolase C) parasagittal zonation of Purkinje cells is noted as organizing associated interneuron zones. Not a molecular-layer interneuron.

name: Cerebellar basket cell (molecular layer interneuron)
anatomy_mentioned: inner/lower third of the molecular layer
perisomatic baskets around Purkinje cell somata
pinceau around Purkinje cell axon initial segment
morphology_summary: Early-born molecular-layer interneuron populating the lower molecular layer; axons converge to enwrap Purkinje cell somata as the 'basket' and form specialized pinceau terminals around the Purkinje axon initial segment (5-7 basket axons per pinceau); each basket cell contacts multiple Purkinje cells in the same sagittal plane. Basket-versus-stellate identity lies on a morphological continuum.
ephys_summary: Provides feed-forward and lateral GABAergic inhibition to Purkinje somata/AIS, controlling Purkinje firing rate; basket-cell inhibition loss changes Purkinje firing rate and decreases complex-spike rate; electrically and chemically coupled to other MLIs with sagittally biased network structure.
subtypes_noted: Classically split from stellate cells by laminar position and axonal target, but the basket/stellate division is a morphological continuum, not absolute. Basket-cell pinceaux are further organized into zonal modules of distinct pinceau sizes aligned with Purkinje-cell functional zones (Zhou et al., 2020). Maps imperfectly onto transcriptomic MLI1/MLI2 classes.

name: Cerebellar stellate cell (molecular layer interneuron)
anatomy_mentioned: outer/upper third of the molecular layer
axons terminate on smooth shafts of Purkinje cell dendrites
morphology_summary: Later-born molecular-layer interneuron integrating into the upper molecular layer; axons innervate Purkinje cell distal dendritic shafts exclusively; each stellate cell contacts multiple Purkinje cells in the same sagittal plane. Shares a ventricular-zone progenitor pool with basket cells and lies on the same morphological continuum.
ephys_summary: Provides GABAergic dendritic inhibition shaping Purkinje dendritic integration and simple-spike patterning; loss of stellate-cell inhibition alters simple-spike pattern and increases complex-spike rate; participates in structured interneuron-interneuron chemical and electrical networks.
subtypes_noted: Classically distinguished from basket cells by upper-ML position and dendritic (not somatic) targeting, but division is a continuum. Does not map cleanly onto transcriptomic MLI1/MLI2 classes.

name: Cerebellar candelabrum cell (Purkinje-layer interneuron)
anatomy_mentioned: Purkinje cell layer (small soma near PCL)
dendrites extending toward the pial surface through the molecular layer
beaded axons making local synapses within the molecular layer
morphology_summary: Molecularly distinct GABAergic interneuron with a small soma near the Purkinje cell layer, dendrites extending pially through the molecular layer, and local beaded axons ramifying within the molecular layer; present across all cerebellar lobules and reported as the most abundant Purkinje-layer interneuron; neither MLI nor Golgi cell.
ephys_summary: High input resistance renders firing highly sensitive to synaptic inputs; excited by mossy fibers and granule cells and strongly inhibited by Purkinje cells; in turn inhibits molecular-layer interneurons, forming an inhibitory ring (PC inhibits CC, CC inhibits MLI, leading to PC disinhibition).
subtypes_noted: Identified as a molecularly distinct type by snRNAseq (Kozareva et al., 2020; Osorno et al., 2021); distinct from MLIs and Golgi cells. No subtypes described.

name: Molecular layer interneuron transcriptomic classes MLI1 / MLI2 (class I / class II)
anatomy_mentioned: molecular layer (both classes span the full thickness as a morphological continuum)
morphology_summary: Two molecularly and functionally distinct MLI types that both span a continuous morphological gradient through the thickness of the molecular layer, so they do not correspond one-to-one to the classical basket/stellate shape categories.
ephys_summary: MLI1 primarily inhibit Purkinje cells, are electrically coupled to each other, fire synchronously on the millisecond timescale in vivo, and synchronously pause Purkinje firing; MLI2 are not electrically coupled, primarily inhibit MLI1 (disinhibiting Purkinje cells), and gate cerebellum-dependent learning. The two classes differ markedly in spontaneous firing, excitability, and electrical coupling.
subtypes_noted: MLI1 and MLI2 (Kozareva et al., 2020) correspond to class I and class II (Lowenstein et al., 2022); proposed as the underlying cell-type structure that the basket/stellate morphological categories only partially capture. Purkinje collaterals preferentially target MLI2 over MLI1 (Lackey et al., 2025).
